sub: Named after “the dominion” (al-mulk) in ayah 1; also called Tabārak
theme: Allah owns and controls everything, created life and death as a test, and built a flawless universe. Its signs all point to Him, and those who ignore the warner will admit their mistake too late.
story: No report says exactly when it was revealed, but its style marks it as one of the earliest surahs revealed in Makkah. Like other early surahs, it presents the whole message briefly, to wake heedless people and make them think.

The Makkan deniers ignored the warnings, asked mockingly when the promised Day would come, and wished for the death of the Prophet ﷺ and his companions. The surah answers them with signs from the sky, the earth, the birds and their own water.

The Prophet ﷺ said a surah of thirty ayat intercedes for its reciter until he is forgiven: Tabārak alladhī bi-yadihi al-mulk. It is also called the protector that rescues from the punishment of the grave.

sections.title: Look again: no flaw in creation
sections.meaning: Allah is blessed and all dominion is in His hand. He created death and life to test who does best. He built seven heavens in layers with no flaw: look again and again, and your eyes come back tired. The nearest heaven has lamps that also strike the devils.
points: All dominion is in His hand; He can do anything
Death and life created to test who is best in deeds
Seven layered heavens: look again, you’ll find no crack
Stars as lamps and as missiles against the devils
sections.matters: It sets the frame for the whole surah: Allah owns everything, and life is a test of quality, not quantity. His flawless creation is the first proof the surah offers.
sections.story: No specific incident. The surah opens with proofs from creation before any warning.
explained: Tabārak: Allah is highest and full of blessing, and all dominion is in His hand. He brought death and life into being to test people. It says “best in deeds”, not “most deeds”: what counts is sincere, correct work and staying away from what He forbade.

He raised seven heavens in layers. Search the sky for a crack, then look again and again: your sight comes back worn out, having found nothing. The nearest heaven is adorned with stars, and flames from them are hurled at devils who try to eavesdrop. The Blaze awaits them.
teaches: The quality of deeds matters more than their number.
Death is part of the test, so remember it often.
Reflect on creation; it points to the Creator.
He is Mighty, yet forgives whoever turns back to Him.
sections.hook: Ayah 1 gives the name (al-mulk). “Return your vision” comes twice (3, 4). Ar-Raḥmān first appears in ayah 3 and returns in 19, 20 and 29.

sections.title: The keepers ask: did no warner come?
sections.meaning: Those who deny their Lord face Hell. It roars and boils, almost bursting with rage. Each group thrown in is asked whether no warner came. They admit he came and they denied him. Had they listened or thought, they wouldn’t be there. They confess, too late.
points: Hell for the deniers: it roars and boils as they are thrown in
Nearly bursting with rage; “Did no warner come?” “Yes, we denied”
If only we had listened or reasoned
They confess: away with the people of the Blaze
sections.matters: It shows Allah’s justice: no one is punished until a warner has come. The deniers’ own confession proves the warning was clear, and that the cure was simply to listen and think.
sections.story: No specific incident. After the proofs from creation, it shows where denying them leads.
explained: For those who disbelieve in their Lord is Hell, a terrible end. As they are thrown in, they hear its shahīq, a dreadful roar, while it boils. It almost tears itself apart with rage at them.

Each time a group is thrown in, its keepers ask, as a rebuke: “Did no warner come to you?” They admit: “Yes, but we denied him and said Allah sent down nothing.” They wish they had listened and used their minds. They confess, but confession no longer helps. Suḥqan: far from mercy.
teaches: Allah never punishes before sending a warner.
Listening and thinking are the paths to guidance.
Regret after the chance has passed doesn’t help.
Take warnings seriously now, while they still benefit.
sections.hook: “The Blaze” (as-saʿīr) ends ayat 5, 10 and 11. “Warner” (nadhīr) comes twice, in 8 and 9: the question, then the answer.

sections.title: He knows what the heart hides
sections.meaning: Those who fear their Lord unseen, even when no one is watching, will have forgiveness and a great reward. Speak secretly or openly: He knows what is inside the chests. How could the Creator not know what He made?
points: Fearing Allah in private: forgiveness and a great reward
Secret or public, He knows what is in the hearts
The One who created knows: al-Laṭīf, al-Khabīr
sections.matters: It gives the true basis of good conduct: fearing Allah even where no one sees. Right after the Fire it shows the other outcome, and why hiding anything from Allah is pointless.
sections.story: The idolaters used to speak against the Prophet ﷺ, and Jibrīl would tell him what they said. So they told each other: “Keep your talk quiet, so Muhammad’s God won’t hear.” Ayah 13 was revealed about this.
explained: After the people of the Fire come the people of forgiveness: those who fear their Lord bil-ghayb, unseen, when only Allah sees them. They avoid sin and do good in private, and they receive forgiveness and a great reward.

Whisper or speak aloud, it is all the same to Him. He knows the intentions inside the chests, let alone words. He created everything, so how could He not know it? He is al-Laṭīf, whose knowledge reaches the finest secret, and al-Khabīr, fully aware.
teaches: Who you are in private is the real test.
Your intentions are fully known to Allah.
The Creator knows His creation inside out.
sections.hook: Page 562 ends at ayah 12, and page 563 opens with ayah 13. Ayah 13 sets secret against open speech; ayah 14 ends with two names, al-Laṭīf al-Khabīr.

sections.title: Feeling safe on a tame earth?
sections.meaning: Allah made the earth easy to live on: walk its paths and eat His provision, and remember the return to Him. Do you feel safe that He won’t make it swallow you, or send a storm of stones? Earlier nations denied and were punished. Look at the birds: only ar-Raḥmān holds them up.
points: The earth made tame: walk, eat, and remember the resurrection
Safe from the earth swallowing you, or a storm of stones?
Earlier nations denied; see how severe My reproach was
Birds spread and fold their wings; only ar-Raḥmān holds them
sections.matters: It turns the everyday into a warning. The ground under you and the air above you are held steady by Allah alone, so feeling safe while denying Him is a delusion.
sections.story: No specific incident. It points to everyday signs, the ground, the sky and the birds, that people take for granted.
explained: Allah made the earth dhalūl, like a calm animal that lets you ride even on its shoulders: firm enough to build on, soft enough to farm and dig. Walk its paths seeking a living, eat from His provision, and remember you will rise again to Him. Effort and trust in Allah go together.

Yet the same earth could swallow you and shake, or a wind could hurl stones at you. Earlier nations denied and felt His reproach. Look up at the birds, wings spread and folding: only ar-Raḥmān keeps them in the air. He sees everything.
teaches: Work for your living, and still rely on Allah.
Never feel safe from Allah’s punishment.
The fate of past nations is a lesson for us.
Ordinary things like birds in flight are signs of Allah.
sections.hook: It opens the second ruku. “Do you feel secure” (a-amintum) begins both 16 and 17, each with “He who is above”. The section moves from the ground (15) to birds above (19).

sections.title: Who else could help or feed you?
sections.meaning: No army can defend you except ar-Raḥmān, and no one can feed you if He holds back. Is someone stumbling on his face better guided than someone walking upright? Allah gave you hearing, sight and hearts. The deniers ask when the Day comes; when they see it near, their faces darken.
points: No army can help you, and no one can feed you but Him
Stumbling on his face, or walking upright on a straight path?
He made you, gave you hearing, sight and hearts, and will gather you
“When is this promise?” When they see it near, faces darken
sections.matters: It strips away every false support: armies, provision, idols. Then it names the real gifts, hearing, sight and understanding, and warns that those who mock the Day will face it.
sections.story: No specific incident. The deniers’ question “When is this promise?” (25) is answered: only Allah knows the time, and the Prophet ﷺ is only a warner.
explained: Who could be your army against ar-Raḥmān, or feed you if He cut off the rain? No one. Still the disbelievers push on in arrogance and flee the truth. Picture two walkers: one bent over, stumbling on his face, lost; the other upright on a straight road. That is the disbeliever and the believer, here and on the Day.

Allah brought you into being and gave you hearing, sight and hearts, yet you rarely thank Him by using them to obey. He spread you over the earth and will gather you back. They ask when; only Allah knows, and the Prophet ﷺ is only a clear warner. When they see it close, their faces darken.
teaches: Only Allah can protect or provide.
Use your hearing, sight and mind to find the truth.
Thank Allah by using His gifts to obey Him.
The Day’s timing is Allah’s; our task is to prepare.
sections.hook: “Or who is it…” (amman hādhā) opens both 20 and 21. “Say” (qul) opens 23, 24 and 26, then every ayah of the last section. Page 564 starts at ayah 27.

sections.title: Who will bring your water back?
sections.meaning: The deniers hoped the Prophet ﷺ and the believers would perish. Say: whether Allah destroys us or has mercy on us, who will save you from a painful punishment? We believe in ar-Raḥmān and rely on Him, and you will know who is astray. And if your water sank away, who would bring it back?
points: Our death won’t save you from punishment
We believe in ar-Raḥmān and rely on Him
If your water sank away, who could bring it flowing?
sections.matters: The surah ends by turning the question back on the deniers: stop waiting for the believers’ ruin and look to your own rescue. The final image, water vanishing underground, shows how completely every life depends on Allah.
sections.story: The Makkan disbelievers cursed the Prophet ﷺ and wished for the death of him and his companions. Ayah 28 answers them: our fate does not change yours.
explained: The deniers kept waiting for the Prophet ﷺ and his followers to die. The reply: whether Allah takes us or has mercy on us, it won’t help you. Who will shield you from the punishment you have earned? Only repentance can.

Our state is clear: we believe in ar-Raḥmān and put our trust in Him, and soon you will see who was clearly lost. Then one last question to ponder: if the water in your wells sank deep into the earth, who could bring you flowing water? Only Allah.
teaches: Worry about your own salvation, not others’ downfall.
Faith and trust in Allah go together.
Every drink of water is a gift from Allah.
sections.hook: All three ayat open with “Say” (qul), and 28 and 30 both start “Have you considered” (a-raʾaytum). The surah ends on page 564, where Al-Qalam also begins.

groups.text: All dominion is Allah’s. He created death and life to test who does best.
Seven heavens without a flaw. Look again and again: your eyes return tired, finding nothing.
Stars adorn the nearest sky and strike the devils, who also face the Blaze.
Hell for those who deny: it roars, boils and nearly bursts. Its keepers ask each group: did no warner come?
They admit they denied him. If only they had listened or reasoned. They confess, and are sent far from mercy.
Those who fear their Lord unseen receive forgiveness and a great reward.
Secret or open, Allah knows what the hearts hold. How could the Creator not know?
Allah made the earth easy to live on: walk it, eat His provision, and remember the return.
Do you feel safe from the earth swallowing you, or a storm of stones? Earlier nations learned.
Birds spread and fold their wings above them; only the Most Merciful holds them up.
No army can protect you from Allah, and no one can provide if He holds back. Yet they persist in arrogance.
Is one who stumbles on his face better guided than one walking upright on a straight path?
He created you, gave you hearing, sight and hearts, spread you over the earth, and will gather you.
They ask when the promise comes. Only Allah knows. When they see it near, their faces darken.
Whether Allah destroys the believers or spares them, who will save the deniers? We trust the Most Merciful.
If your water sank into the earth, who could bring you flowing water?

1.explain: Tabārak: Allah is exalted and His blessing is vast. Al-mulk, the dominion of the heavens, the earth and the Hereafter, is in His hand. He does as He wills, and no one can overturn His decree.

2.explain: Death comes first: things were lifeless before being given life, and death is the strongest reminder. Aḥsanu ʿamalan: best in deed, meaning sincere and correct, not simply most. Al-ʿAzīz al-Ghafūr: Mighty, yet Forgiving to those who repent.

3.explain: Sabʿa samāwātin ṭibāqā: seven heavens stacked in layers. Tafāwut: any mismatch or inconsistency. Fuṭūr: cracks or rifts. Look up and check for yourself.

4.explain: Karratayn: again and again. Your sight comes back khāsiʾ, defeated at finding no flaw, and ḥasīr, worn out from searching.

5.explain: Maṣābīḥ, lamps, are the stars. Flames taken from them are thrown at devils who try to overhear the heavens; the stars themselves stay in place. In the Hereafter the devils face as-saʿīr, the Blaze.

6.explain: Not only the devils: those who disbelieve in their Lord also face Jahannam. Biʾsa al-maṣīr: the worst place to end up.

7.explain: Ulqū: thrown in, in disgrace. Shahīq: a harsh, ugly roaring sound. Tafūr: it boils, churning them like a few seeds in a lot of boiling water.

8.explain: Tamayyazu min al-ghayẓ: its parts almost tear apart from rage. Its keepers ask each fawj, each group, not for information but as a rebuke: didn’t a warner come?

9.explain: They admit the warner came. They denied him, denied that Allah revealed anything at all, and even called the messengers deeply misguided.

10.explain: Nasmaʿ, naʿqil: had we truly listened to understand, or reasoned to reflect, we would not be here. They admit they used neither.

11.explain: They confess their sin when confession no longer helps. Suḥqan: may they be far, far away from Allah’s mercy.

12.explain: Bil-ghayb: fearing Allah when no one else sees, so they avoid sin and obey in private. Maghfirah: their sins wiped away. Ajr kabīr: a great reward, Paradise.

13.explain: Asirrū aw ijharū: hide it or say it aloud, it is the same to Him. Dhāt aṣ-ṣudūr: what the chests hold, intentions and thoughts. If He knows those, He surely knows words.
13.why: The idolaters used to speak against the Prophet ﷺ, and Jibrīl told him what they said. So they said to one another: “Keep your talk secret, so Muhammad’s God won’t hear.” This ayah was revealed about them.

14.explain: Alā yaʿlamu man khalaq: doesn’t the One who created know, or doesn’t He know those He created? Al-Laṭīf: His knowledge reaches the subtlest secret, and He is gentle with His servants. Al-Khabīr: fully informed.

15.explain: Dhalūl: submissive, easy to walk and build on. Manākib: its paths and sides (literally “shoulders”). Travel and trade, eat from His provision, but an-nushūr, the rising from the graves, is coming.

16.explain: Man fī as-samāʾ: He who is above. The earth could sink with you and tamūr, heave and sway until it closes over you. He holds this back out of patience, giving respite.

17.explain: Ḥāṣib: a violent wind carrying stones, like the one that struck the people of Lūṭ. Then you would know how true My warning (nadhīr) was, but too late.

18.explain: Nations before them denied too. Nakīr: My reproach, the punishment that destroyed them. So beware of meeting the same end.

19.explain: Ṣāffāt: wings spread out; yaqbiḍna: folding them in. Birds are heavy, yet only ar-Raḥmān holds them aloft, by making the air carry them. He sees what suits every creature.

20.explain: Jund: an army or protection. Who could defend you if ar-Raḥmān willed you harm? No one. Ghurūr: the disbelievers are fooled into thinking punishment won’t reach them.

21.explain: Who would feed you if He withheld His rizq, such as the rain? No one can. Lajjū fī ʿutuwwin wa nufūr: they persist in arrogance and in running from the truth.

22.explain: Mukibban ʿalā wajhih: bent over, stumbling on his face, lost. Sawiyyan: upright on a straight path. The disbeliever and the believer. The disbeliever will even be gathered walking on his face; the One who gave legs can do that.

23.explain: Anshaʾakum: He brought you into being from nothing. Hearing, sight and afʾidah, hearts, are the tools of knowledge. Qalīlan mā tashkurūn: how little you thank Him by using them to obey.

24.explain: Dharaʾakum: He spread you across the earth, with all your languages and colours. As He scattered you, He will gather you back for judgement.

25.explain: The deniers mockingly ask: when will this promise of resurrection happen, if you are truthful? As if knowing its date were the proof of its truth.

26.explain: Knowledge of its time is with Allah alone. The Prophet ﷺ is only a nadhīr mubīn, a clear warner: his duty is to convey, and he did.

27.explain: Zulfah: near. When they see it close, their faces turn dark with grief, and they are told: this is what you used to call for. Usually taken as the Hereafter; one view says Badr.

28.explain: Araʾaytum: have you considered? If Allah destroys me and those with me, as you hope, or has mercy on us, who will protect the disbelievers? No one. Wishing for our ruin can’t save you.
28.why: The disbelievers of Makkah cursed the Prophet ﷺ and wished for the destruction of him and the believers. This ayah answers them.

29.explain: Āmannā bihi wa ʿalayhi tawakkalnā: we believe in Him and rely on Him in everything. Trust is named because every deed depends on it. You will see who is fī ḍalālin mubīn, clearly astray.

30.explain: Ghawran: sunk deep into the earth, beyond hands and buckets. Maʿīn: flowing, visible water. Only Allah can bring it. It is reported that after this ayah one should say: Allāhu rabbul-ʿālamīn.
